newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Rains slow down Serbia wheat harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rains slow down Serbia wheat harvest.

text.p: Rains and hail in some parts of Serbia over the past few days have slowed wheat harvesting and could reduce yields in those areas by several percent, Belgrade media reported on Tuesday.
"When weather is as rainy as it is now, wheat yields are several percent lower every day," Srbislav Dencic of the Novi Sad Institute for Crop Farming was quoted as saying by the daily Nasa Borba.
According to Dencic, it was impossible to say how much wheat would be lost since detailed information was needed on the levels of precipitation and hail.
"In any case, such weather postpones harvesting and yield could generally be 10 to 15 percent lower," Dencic said.

The highest rainfall since Saturday, with hail in places, was registered in the granary of Vojvodina, where wheat harvesting began a few days ago on some 366,000 hectares of the total 800,000 ha under wheat in Yugoslavia.
Vojvodina is expected to account for some 1.358 million of Yugoslavia's total wheat crop of 2.75 million tonnes.
However, the rains may benefit spring crops such as maize.
Cooler, cloudy and windy weather with occasional showers will continue until Thursday, when a sunny and dry spell with a slight rise in temperatures is expected, forecasters said.
